descriptionChirho: To move from inside a place to outside, physically exiting or leaving a location such as a house, city, or gathering.
To leave a place or person with emphasis on departure or withdrawal rather than the act of passing through an exit.
Imperative use commanding someone or something (often an unclean spirit) to come out or go out, as in exorcism or authoritative dismissal.
To go out in the sense of proceeding forth, issuing, or spreading abroad, as of news, reports, or proclamations emanating from a source.
